Repeated operations can make CAE user boring and uncomfortable. The iterative work without automation cannot be completed within a desired duration. Manual operation by human can create mistakes. In depth CAE trainings can be required if modelling is complicated. Each firm has its own design rule/process, design specification/template, etc. thus customized UI specific to each user will be more convenient and helpful.
documents.s: Background problems in daily CAE work

documents.t: To solve the above problems and meet the requirements from our diverged users, PSJ (Python Scripting for Jupiter) is developed, with our 4F moto:

With PSJ, you would have these below features: Jupiter functions in Python script Incorporate with Jupiter’s powerful Pre/Post functions Connect with other software Compatible with Python 3.x and its vast libraries GUI Command Builder: Easy creation of GUI dialog equivalent to Jupiter built-in's Customized IDE: With powerful predicting tips, programming support functions Customized Shell: Error output for debugging More information To know all PSJ solutions, please check out our dedicated sample applications.
Customized Shell (or Python API window) can be displayed by checking the checkbox in Home » Window » Python API.

Python commands and execution results are displayed in this area. Black color: PSJ-command information Blue color: Script execution result Red color: Error message Useful tip User can double mouse click on error line information to jump to the specified line in the Customized IDE.

User can run PSJ line by line directly using this Command Line Interface (CLI). Copy ^ Ctrl + C and Paste ^ Ctrl + V operations are supported (for single or multiple lines command) Previous commands can be navigated back and forth using the ↑ Up or ↓ Down key button. User can also double click on a line in the Log window to quickly copy and paste the command to this CLI Auto-fill keywords for Macro, PSJ-Command and PSJ-Utility using ⇥ Tab key. After a keyword is filled, user can use ^ Ctrl + ↑ Up to go backward or ^ Ctrl + ↓ Down to go forward to the near keyword

This section will introduce Jupiter's customized IDE for PSJ, which can be accessed from the Python ribbon. Currently, this built-in IDE supports: Code highlighter, Auto completion, Tooltip for built in function or user-defined function and Group block of script (Collapse/Expand).

Built-in Python keywords and PSJ API are highlighted in different color for better visualization. The highlighted data is stored in the database folder. In addition, when user double-clicks a word, the same word is highlighted (yellow).

This IDE supports auto-completion. For example, if user types Geometry.Me, a list box will appear and show words that start with Me. The auto-completion data is stored in the database folder and supporting the following: All words in the IDE Python keywords PSJ-Utility PSJ-Command

This IDE supports showing tooltips. For example, if user enters JPT.ClearLog(, a tooltip showing the JPT.ClearLog document is displayed. The docstring from user's defined function is also displayed. The tooltip data is stored in the database folder.
This IDE supports code block grouping (a portion of code can be shown or hidden)

Name Description Shortcut key New Make a new document ^ Ctrl + N Open Open a saved Python script file. (uer can also drag & drop Python file to the IDE window) ^ Ctrl + O Save Save the Python script file ^ Ctrl + S Save As Save the Python script file with another name ^ Ctrl + E Exit Close the IDE ^ Ctrl + Q

(if user selects some words before executing this function, initial search value will be added with selected words) ^ Ctrl + F Comment Insert the comment tag # before the selected script ^ Ctrl + K Toggle Comment Switch between comment and comment cancellation ^ Ctrl + T Go To Line Go to a specific line in the script ^ Ctrl + G Find And Replace Find and replace the specific characters in the script. (if user selects some words before executing this function, initial search value will be added with selected words) ^ Ctrl + H Convert to Upper Case Convert selected text to upper case ^ Ctrl + ⇧ Shift + U Convert to Lower Case Convert selected text to lower case ^ Ctrl + U Insert Tab Insert a tab to current cursor. A Double specifying bias factor, which could be the equal ratio r (if iBiasProgression is 0) or the equal difference (if iBiasProgression is 1). This parameter can only be used only when bEnableMeshCount is True and iBiasMethod is 2 or 3. The default value is 0.0.

An Integer specifying bias method. This parameter is mainly used for local mesh setting on Edge type entity. The number of node to set up is specified in iNodeCount, with bias factor dBiasFactor and progression method iBiasProgression. This parameter and can be one of the following 0: Equal: no bias is set up, nodes are equally distributed. 1: Bias: bias is set up, nodes are distributed so that dense area starts from node with id iBiasNodeId. 2: Bias-sides: bias is set up, nodes are distributed so that dense area starts from both 2 bounding nodes of the edge. 3: Bias-center: bias is set up, nodes are distributed so that dense area is at the middle distance of the edge. This parameter is used only when bEnableMeshCount is True. The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying bias progression method, which can be one of the following: 0: Geometric: distance of nodes will increase by an equal ratio r, where r is bias factor dBiasFactor. For example, when r = 2, if distance between first node and second node is 1, distance between second and third node will be 1 * r = 2, and the next distance will be 4. 1: Arithmetic: distance of nodes will increase by an equal difference d, where d is bias factor dBiasFactor. For example, when d = 2, if distance between first node and second node is 1, distance between second and third node will be 1 + d = 3, and the next distance will be 5. This parameter is used only when bEnableMeshCount is True and iBiasMethod is 2 or 3. The default value is 0.

documents.t: Installation by folder copy (up to V4.0.x) Check the Python version of Jupiter (in V4.0.2 is 3.6.3). Install the same Python version to your machine. Install the module using the pip command in Python to your machine. -> A module folder will be created under the \Lib\site-package folder in the Python installation folder. Copy the created folder under the Jupiter-Pre installation folder \Lib\site-packages. Install with pip (V4.1 or later) Open a command prompt with administrator mode Move to Jupiter installation folder Enter the following command: python -m pip install <module> warning If you update Jupiter, the additional installed libraries will basically remain. However, if the Python version of Jupiter has been updated, the library may stop working. In that case, please reinstall the appropriate version of the library.

To develop PSJ, user can use Jupiter built-in IDE, other text editor, or Visual Studio Code from Microsoft (called VSCode for short).

VSCode is an open-source text editor, with the ability to install various extensions to make your Python development faster and easier. Besides all the features of the current Jupiter built-in IDE, VSCode also provides: A debugger An AI co-pilot Linkage to online/local Scripting API document Linting (Hint for fixing the code) caution This is beta version, please do not use for real application. If you have any feedback or question, please contact us.

Install VSCode extension for code highlight, suggestion and snippet via this link Install a Python library for Jupiter-Connection/Debugger using below command (change the link in double quote below if Jupiter was installed in different location): python -m pip install "C:\Program Files\TechnoStar\Jupiter_5.0\tools\jupiterutils-3.9.tar.gz" In VSCode, before writing PSJ script, remember to import the installed module using from jupiterutils import *

To get the most out of PSJ, start by reviewing a few introductory topics: Intro Videos - Begin your journey with PSJ through these introductory videos. Tutorials - Start making real PSJ applications. PSJ Structure - Understand PSJ basic structure. Scripting API - Read our Scripting API manual (or you can also use our search function at the top right corner). PSJ Extensions - Get to know what PSJ support you writing the script more effectively. External IDE - For writing a complicated script with connection to other software, we recommend user to use Visual Studio Code extension.

GUI Command Builder is an interactive builder of PSJ-GUI, help making Jupiter dialog or wizard by Drag & Drop operations. User hence does not need to know Python programming language to make UI components in Jupiter. GUI Command Builder can be easily accessed from Python ribbon. The main application has below menu and windows:

Perform operations related to the creation of dialogs and wizards. Icon Name Description Shortcut Key Make a new dialog Clear the being created settings and open a new environment F5 Open an existing database Open and load a database file F4 Save dialog settings to database Save the being created dialog settings to an external database file F6 Save dialog settings to new database Save the being created dialog settings to a new database file F7 Undo Undo the previously executed operation Redo Redo the previously cancelled operation Show or hide code window Switch showing or hiding the code window F1 Preview dialog Display a preview of the being created dialog F2 Save dialog to customer folder Save the dialog to the PSJ Command folder and display it in Jupiter's ribbon F3 Help Display a short tutorial (being created)
In this tab, user can design a custom dialog.

Contain all the components used to create dialogs and wizards. Icon Name Description Layout Create a layout to arrange components inside GroupBox Create a group box which can contain some components TabWnd Create a tab container TabItem Create a tab inside the tab container Label Create a label TextBox Create a text box RichEditCtrl Create a text box that can be entered in various data formats and multiple lines ComboBox Create a combo box ListBox Create a list box CheckBox Create a check box RadioButton Create a radio button Button Create a button ImageCtrl Create an image container Spin Create a spin button Slide Bar Create a slide bar Separator Create a separator line Browser Create a open file/folder selection Table Create a table PagesCtrl Create a page container (used for wizard) PageItem Create a page inside the page container (used for wizard)

All components in use are displayed in a tree format. User can change the position (using icons or Drag & Drop operations), duplicate or delete components. Icon Name Description Move item out of current container Move the selected component out of the current container which it is being belong to Move item into next container Move the selected component into the above container Move item forward one level Move the selected component up one level but still inside the current container Move item backward one level Move the selected component down one level but still inside the current container Copy item and insert it Duplicate the selected component Delete selected item Delete the selected component Expand all tree nodes Expand all subtrees Collapse all tree nodes Collapse all subtrees

Display all properties of the selected component. The settings of the dialog created can also be set from the Properties window. By selecting a component in the Hierarchy window, user can change its parameters in this Properties window.
In this tab, user can integrate the PSJ automation script to the current dialog.
Define location of the PSJ script and main function. Name Description Module Location of the PSJ script Function Main function which will be run after Apply or OK button is pressed
A simple text editor showing the selected PSJ file for user's edition or confirmation.
Show all the current component names defined in the GUI Builder tab. User can double click on the component name to quickly insert it the current cursor location in the Script window.

Equivalent to Macro, but PSJ-Command is polished to be compact, easy to write and fully Python compatible. This new PSJ feature is introduced from Jupiter version 5.

PSJ-Command's functions are named after Class-based format and Jupiter’s ribbon. For example, making a cube with default input values: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0, 0, 0], dlLength=[0.01, 0.01, 0.01], ilAxialNodes=[10, 10, 10], strName="Cube_1", iPartColor=7105764, crLocalCoordinate=None) CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) PSJ-Command's arguments follow our standard naming convention

PSJ-Command's parameters are neglected if the default values are taken. For example, making a cube with default input values: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cube() CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0)

PSJ-Command is easier to read thanks to its explicit definitions. For example, imprinting a line on a face between 2 points: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Edge.Line(dllPoints=[[0.0078, 0, 0.01], [0.0023, 0.01, 0.01]], crlFaces=[Face(26)]) ImprintLineS([[7.8, 0, 10], [2.2, 10, 10]], [6:26], 1)

PSJ-Command has return value which can make the code looks more Pythonic. For example, deleting 2 cubes just created: PSJ-Command Macro cube1 = Geometry.Part.Cube() cube2 = Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0.01, 0.0, 0.0], strName="Cube_2", iPartColor=6409934) Geometry.DeleteEntity.Part(crlParts=[cube1, cube2]) CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) CreateCube([10, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_2", 6409934, 0:0) DeletePartCr([3:1, 3:2])

PSJ-Command has error handling built-in which can help developer found the bug faster and easier. For example, inputting a code with a wrong format as below: # Below input has wrong name in the second parameter Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0.01, 0.0, 0.0], strame="Cube_1") After running the above code, the error will be shown in the Python API window: note PSJ interpreter will raise error (exception) when it can not find an entity in database (a database query error). With a wrong input argument (entity ID) then it can lead to a query error rather than return a failed result.
PSJ-Command is fully supported by our customized IDE or VSCode extensions. Read more To get the full list of available PSJ-Command, please refer to the Scripting API.

A Boolean specifying whether to use the settings of Result Reference. If bResultReference=True, the settings of Result Reference arguments will be valid to use. The default value is False.

An Integer specifying the method to separate file. This option allows to separate information into many exported ADX files by the specified type. If iSeparateFile=0, this option would export only 1 ADX file contains all information of all bodies/parts in the model (ModelInfo, Unit, Geometry, LBCs, Process Sequence,...). If iSeparateFile=1, this option would export 2 ADX files, which the first ADX file has same name as analysis Job will contain general information (such as ModelInfo, Unit, LBCs, Job name, Process Sequence, other settings of ADVC Structure analysis). When the last one ADX file which has suffix name "_model", contains Geometry information (such as Node, Part, Element,...). If iSeparateFile=2, this option would export ADX files, which each body/part in model would be written individually Geometry information, Group in model would be written in another file, while other information would be written in the ADX file has same name as analysis Job. If iSeparateFile=3, this option would export ADX file that write information of selected part/body. If selection does not have at least a specific body/part, Jupiter would write all bodies/part (same option as iSeparateFile=0). If iSeparateFile=4, this option would export 1 ADX file contains LBCs information of the chosen LBCs. The default value is 0.

A Boolean specifying whether to export all related Load Boundary Condition. This argument is to be used when iSeparateFile=3. If True, this option would export ADX file contains related information to LBCs such as Contact, Connection RBE, Bolt Pretension,... The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying whether to use entity name in exported file or not. If True, this option would export ADX file that write Entity name to Geometry information such as Part, Face,... If iLoadType=1: Load, which will export ADX file stores all Loads, BCs as a 1 Load case only. The default value is 1.

Create and export the ADVC (*.adx) file for the Structure analysis.
A String specifying the job name of ADVC analysis. This name would be the name of analysis job in Assembly Tree and the name of the ADX file after exported. The default value is "".
A String specifying the description for ADVC analysis job. The description would write in the ADX file, where contents will be written below ModelInfo. The default value is "".
A List of Cursor specifying the list of ADVC process sequence. This argument controls the Process solution type and its setting information depended on solution type. The default value is [].
A List of Cursor specifying the list of element location. The model contains element group such as 3D Element, 2D Element, 1D Element to use this argument. The default value is [].
A List of Cursor specifying the list of node location. The model contains node group to use this argument. The default value is [].

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the write group option which output a selected group of faces, elements, nodes as Surface Segment, Element Set and Node set respectively. If True, ADX file would contained group information such as Part, Face, Element(3D,2D,1D), Node,... If False, ADX won't write group information. The default value is False.

A Cursor specifying an existing ADVC job in Assembly Tree to modify it. If this parameter is used, the specified ADVC job will be modified. If it is left None, a new ADVC job will be created. The default value is None.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the Result Reference option is defined or not. If True, this option will allow to active settings of Result Reference. The settings of Result Reference arguments will be valid to use. If False, this option will be disable settings of Result Reference. In this case, the settings of Result Reference arguments will be ignored even though User has set value or not. The default value is False.

An Integer specifying the separate file type. This option allows to separate information into many exported ADX files by selected type. If iSeparateFile=0: None, this option would export only 1 ADX file contains all information of all bodies/parts in the model (ModelInfo, Unit, Geometry, LBCs, Process Sequence,...) If iSeparateFile=1: By Model, this option would export 2 ADX files, which the first ADX file has same name as analysis Job will contain general information (such as ModelInfo, Unit, LBCs, Job name, Process Sequence, other settings of ADVC Structure analysis). When the last one ADX file which has suffix name "_model", contains Geometry information (such as Node, Part, Element,...) If iSeparateFile=2: By Body, this option would export ADX files, which each body/part in model would be written individually Geometry information, Group in model would be written in another file, while other information would be written in the ADX file has same name as analysis Job. If iSeparateFile=3: By Selected Body, this option would export ADX file that write information of selected part/body. If selection does not have at least a specific body/part, Jupiter would write all bodies/part (same option as None). If iSeparateFile=4: By Selected LBCs, this option would export 1 ADX file contains LBCs information of the chosen LBCs. The default value is 0.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that export all related Load Boundary Condition. This option could be used when iSeparateFile=3(By Selected Body), if not, this setting is not activated for both True or False. If True, this option would export the ADX file contains related information to LBCs such as Contact, Connection RBE, Bolt Pretension,... If False, this option won't export related information to LBCs such as Contact, Connection RBE, Bolt Pretension,... The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that use entity name in exported file or not. If True, this option would export the ADX file that write Entity name(Name of the Part/Entity) to Geometry information such as Part, Face,... If False, this option would export the ADX file without writing Entities name to Geometry information. The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that the Matrix Solver Parameter is defined ot not. If True, this option will allow to active settings of Matrix Solver Parameter. The settings of Matrix Solver Parameter arguments will be valid to use. If False, this option will be disable settings of Matrix Solver Parameter. In this case, the settings of Matrix Solver Parameter arguments will be ignored even though User has set value or not. The default value is False.

An Integer specifying the precondition type. If iPreconditionType=0: Scaling If iPreconditionType=1: CGCG If iPreconditionType=2: CGCG2 If iPreconditionType=3: CGCG2_Diag If iPreconditionType=4: CGCG2-SOR The default value is 0.
An Integer specifying the matrix structure type. If iMatrixStructure=0: Symmetry If iMatrixStructure=1: Asymmetry The default value is 0.
A List of Cursor specifying the list of targets. The target could be Part or LBCs item. The default value is [].

An Integer specifying the load type uses for analysis. If iLoadType=0: Load Case, which is a group of specific Loads, BCs applies on model. The model could apply many Load Cases which may have same setting of LBCs. Exporting ADX file would write all Load Cases. If iLoadType=1: Load, which will export the ADX file stores all Loads, BCs as a 1 Load case only. The default value is 1.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the same output request for all processes. If True, this option would set same output request (Displacement, Stress, Strain,...) for all defined processes. If False, this option would set output request which will base on user's desired result for each process. The default value is True.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that would delete floating node or not. If True, this option would export an ADX file without writing floating nodes information. If False, this option would export an ADX file with floating nodes information. The default value is True.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that would separate boundary condition. This option could be used when iSeparateFile=3 (By Selected Body), if not, this setting is not activated for both True or False. If True, this option would export an ADX file would write LBCs information. If False, this option won't export an ADX file would write LBCs information. The default value is True.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable checking whether boundary conditions are duplicated or not. If True, this option checks LBCs duplication when export the ADX file. If False, this option won't check LBCs duplication when export the ADX file. The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable automatically assign dummy property option. This option used when model that has not assign property yet. If the model already has property If True, the model would be exported with dummy property for the Part that does not have property. The others Part (which already assigned property) will export with its property setting. If False, the model will export ADX file in case of the model has all property in all Parts, but if there is one Part that does not have property in the model, this option will not export file. The default value is False.
A Cursor specifying the dummy property material for automatically assigning dummy property when export the ADX file. The default value is None.

Create connectors between nodes, edges, and faces according to specified connection types. User selects master/slave targets and the connectors will be created to connect nodes on master/slave targets with each other.

A String specifying the connection name to be created. The default value is "Connector_1".
An Integer specifying the connection method. If iMethod=1, the method is Node to Node. If iMethod=2, the method is Edge to Edge. If iMethod=3, the method is Face to Face. The default value is 1.

An Integer specifying the connection type. If iConnectType=0, the connection type is Parallel. If iConnectType=1, the connection type is Translation. An Integer specifying a node to refer to when determining the coordinate system. If iRefNode=0, reference to the first node. If iRefNode=1, reference to the second node. The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying the option whether or not an element coordinate system is used. If iElemCs=0, do not use element coordinate system. If iElemCs=1, use element coordinate system. The default value is 0.
A Cursor specifying the local coordinate system. The default value is None.
A List of Cursor specifying the table data of elastic property. The default value is [].
A List of Cursor specifying the table data of viscosity characteristics. The default value is [].

A List of Cursor specifying the list of master targets. The targets are nodes when the iMethod is equal to 1. The targets are edges when the iMethod is equal to 2. And the targets are faces when the iMethod is equal to 3. The default value is [].

A List of Cursor specifying the list of slave targets. The targets are nodes when the iMethod is equal to 1. The targets are edges when the iMethod is equal to 2. And the targets are faces when the iMethod is equal to 3. The default value is [].

Define the contact set between the specified group for Abaqus. Create a group with master and slave surfaces beforehand to define the contact in the contact settings.
Connections.Contacts.Abaqus.ManualGroup(...) Ribbon: Connections » Contacts » Abaqus » Manual Group
A String specifying the new Abaqus Contact name. The default value is "ContactAbaqus_1".

An Integer specifying the behavior type of contact definition. The behavior type of contact definition is one of the following: 0: General (Sliding Contact) 1: Tied (Shell-Solid contact) 2: All with self - Automatic contact detection The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying the contact setting target entity. 0: Face to Face - Contact between shell or solid element faces and shell or solid element faces. 1: Node to Face - Contact between node and shell or solid element faces. The default value is 0.

A Double specifying a value to adjust the initial positions of the surfaces specified. This is required when the iTied parameter is used with ON value. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. The default value is 0.0.

A Double specifying a value that is equal to a fraction of the end segment or facet edge length by which Abaqus extends the master surface to avoid numerical round-off errors associated with contact modeling. The value given must lie between 0.0 and 0.2. This parameter affects only node-to-surface contact. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. The default value is 0.0.

A Double specifying the maximum distance by which a point on the slave surface must penetrate the master surface before Abaqus abandons the current increment and tries again with a smaller increment. This parameter does not apply to contact pairs that use the finite-sliding, surface-to-surface contact formulation. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. The default value is 0.0.

An Integer specifying whether to use the small-sliding contact formulation. This parameter is not allowed with self-contact. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. 0: OFF 1: ON The default value is 0.

A Double specifying the degree of smoothing used for element-based master surfaces in the finite-sliding, node-to-surface contact formulation. The value given must lie between 0.0 and 0.5. This parameter does not affect contact pairs with analytical rigid surfaces or contact formulations other than the finite-sliding, node-to-surface contact formulation. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. The default value is 0.0.
An Integer specifying the friction characteristics type. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. 0: None 1: General 2: Lagrange 3: Rough 4: Static & Kinetic The default value is 0.
A Double specifying the first friction coefficient to be defined in terms of slip rate. This argument is used only when iFrictionType=1 or iFrictionType=2. The default value is 0.0.
A Double specifying the second friction coefficient to be defined in terms of slip rate. This argument is used only when iFrictionType=1 or iFrictionType=2. The default value is 0.0.

A Double specifying an optional equivalent shear stress limit, so that regardless of the magnitude of the contact pressure stress, sliding will occur if the magnitude of the equivalent shear stress reaches this value. A value of zero is not allowed. This argument is used only when iFrictionType=1 or iFrictionType=2. The default value is 0.0.
A Double specifying the maximum allowable elastic slip for surface dimension ratio. This argument is used only when iFrictionType=1 or iFrictionType=4. The default value is 0.0.
A Double specifying the static friction coefficient. This argument is used only when iFrictionType=4. The default value is 0.0.
A Double specifying the dynamic friction coefficient. This argument is used only when iFrictionType=4. The default value is 0.0.
A Double specifying the decay coefficient. This argument is used only when iFrictionType=4. The default value is 0.0.
An Integer specifying whether to adjust the position of surfaces in the contact pair. This argument is used only when iContactType=1. The default value is False.
A Double specifying the tolerance of position of surfaces used for adjustment. This argument is used only when bAdjustPosition=1. The default value is 0.0.
An Integer specifying how Abaqus generates the contact constraint coefficients. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. 0: Node to Surface 1: Surface to Surface The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying whether the surfaces in the contact pair are to be tied together for the duration of the analysis. This argument is used only when iContactType=0. 0: Not specified - Not want to tie the surfaces together. 1: ON - Tie the surfaces together. The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying a contact pressure-overclosure relationship. 0: Hard Contact - Pressure-overclosure relationship without physical softening. 1: Exponential - Exponential pressure-overclosure relationship. 2: Linear - Linear pressure-overclosure relationship. 3: Tabular - Piecewise linear pressure-overclosure relationship in tabular form. 4: None The default value is 0.
An Integer specifying whether to allow separation of the two surfaces once contact has been established. This argument is used when iPressureOverclosureType=0. The default value is False.
A Double specifying the slope of the pressure-overclosure curve. This value must be positive and is required when iPressureOverclosureType=2. The default value is 0.0.

A Table Sheet specifying the tabular data of Pressure-Overclosure used for exponential pressure-overclosure relationship. This argument must be specified when iPressureOverclosureType=1 or iPressureOverclosureType=3. The default value is [].

An Integer specifying the contact characteristic definition method of heat conduction. 0: None 1: Clearance Dependency 2: Pressure Dependency 3: Clearance & Pressure Dependency The default value is 0.
A Boolean specifying whether the tabular data have Temperature-Dependent property. The default value is False.
An Integer specifying the number of field variables in the data table. This argument must be specified when iThermalConductanceDef=1 or iThermalConductanceDef=3. The default value is 0.
A Table Sheet specifying the tabular data of clearance dependency. The default value is [].
A Boolean enable/disable using temperature dependency data. The default value is False.
An Integer specifying number of the field variables. The default value is 0.
A Table Sheet specifying the table of pressure dependency. The default value is [].

A List of Pair of Cursor specifying the list or pair of group master face and group slave face. The crplTargets and crContactAbaqus arguments are mutually exclusive. One of them must be specified. The default value is [].

A Cursor specifying an existing Abaqus Contact (Manual Group). If this parameter is used, the specified contact settings will be modified. Otherwise, a new contact settings will be created. The crplTargets and crContactAbaqus arguments are mutually exclusive. One of them must be specified. The default value is None.
An Integer specifying the contact color. The default value is 0.
A Cursor specifying the created contact.

An Integer specifying the flag to indicate if the contact status for a specific sub-case is to start from the final status of the previous subcase. This argument is available to be used if iContactType=0. 0: Starts from previous subcase. 1: Starts from initial state. The default value is 0.

Meshing.CADProjection.Face(...) Ribbon: Meshing » CAD Projection » Face

A Cursor specifying the CAD parts. Faces on selected parts will be the referenced faces for projection. Note that for CAD part, Cursor type will take different format from normal cursor's format. Two parameters are now needed: the former is ID (external id) and the latter is Key (internal id). For example: RefPart((1,2)) means a CAD part with ID (external id) = 1 and Key (internal id) = 2. This is a required input.
A List of Cursor specifying list of meshed faces. Nodes on these faces will be projected onto referenced faces. This is a required input.
A Boolean specifying whether to force projection or not. If True, Jupiter will try to do projection more aggressively, hence may takes more time to finish. The default value is False.
A Boolean specifying whether to project corner nodes or not. If True, corner nodes of elements will be projected. The default value is True.
A Boolean specifying whether to project mid nodes or not. If True, mid nodes of elements will be projected. The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying whether to check ID when projecting or not. If True, nodes (on selected meshed faces) will only be projected to CAD faces (in the selected CAD Parts) whose ID is the same as the meshed face of those nodes. For example, if one node is on face 5, that node will only be projected to CAD face (in selected CAD Parts) with the same ID (i.e. 5). If False, ID check will be skipped, and projection takes place when nodes and CAD faces (in the selected CAD parts) are at the closest distance. The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying the status of the process: True: Projected the nodes of the meshed faces to the CAD (Reference) part. False: Cannot project the nodes of the meshed faces to the CAD (Reference) part.

Renumber the IDs of the model such as Face, Edge, Elements(1D,2D,3D) and Nodes.
A List of RENUMBER_ITEM specifying the renumber information. This is a required input.

A Boolean specifying whether to renumber the assigned-property elements or not. This parameter can only be used when elements(1D, 2D, 3D) are the target to renumber. Other entities namely Faces, Edges, Nodes are not able to use by this argument. If True, only elements to which property is assigned will be renumbered. If False, all existing elements will be renumbered. The default value is True.

A Boolean specifying whether Nodes are needed to renumber from the surface corner first. This parameter can only be used when Nodes are the target to renumber. Other entities are not able to use by this argument. If True, Nodes(vertices) on the corner of Faces would have the first priority to renumber, other Nodes such as mid Nodes, internal Nodes would have lower order when renumber. If False, Nodes(vertices) on the corner of Faces would have same priority with others Nodes The default value is False.
A Boolean specifying whether the process is executed successfully or not: True: The process is executed successfully. False: Cannot execute the function.

A String specifying the path of CSV file. The CSV file must correspond correctly with the model, can not use a different CSV for a different model. This is a required input.

An Integer specifying the conflict strategy. This parameter is used to apply to Share Face/Node case, by choosing the method that assigning ID of Share Face/Nodes would belong to which part. If iConflictStrategy=0: Less ID(<) method, when the Share Face/Nodes existing in model, the ID of them when renumber will belong to the Part has smaller ID. If iConflictStrategy=1: Great ID(<) method, when the Share Face/Nodes existing in model, the ID of them when renumber will belong to the Part has larger ID. The default value is 0.

A Boolean specifying the option to activate the counter update of each model for each component(Nodes, 2D, 3D). The counter is a value that represents the total amount of each component. If True: The counter will update If False: The counter will not update The default value is False.
A Boolean specifying whether the process is executed successfully or not: True: The process is executed successfully. False: Cannot execute the function.

Get elements with loaded results satisfy a condition.
An Enum specifying the PostDataRangeType describing the condition to get the element results. This is a required input.
A Double specifying the referenced value. This is a required input.

A Double specifying the adjustment to the referenced value resultValue: If PostDataRangeType is a scalar type (i.e. EQ, NE, LT, GT, LE, GE), then the range to get the result is from (resultValue - adjustment) to (resultValue + adjustment) If PostDataRangeType is a range type (i.e. IR, OR, IRE, ORE), then the range to get the result is from (resultValue) to (adjustment) The default value is 1E-5.

A Double specifying the adjustment to the base value resultValue: If PostDataRangeType is a scalar type (i.e. EQ, NE, LT, GT, LE, GE), then the range to get the result is from (resultValue - adjustment) to (resultValue + adjustment) If PostDataRangeType is a range type (i.e. IR, OR, IRE, ORE), then the range to get the result is from (resultValue) to (adjustment) The default value is 1E-5.

PSJ is fully featured with tools and utilities, supports user write Python API script for Jupiter with ease: After Jupiter built-in dialog functions execution, Jupiter will also log out a set of Macro and PSJ-Command to represent the same operations, but in a kind of command language. User can use these commands to rerun the same Jupiter operations. In case user wants to query model's database information (e.g. model's name, IDs, color, etc.), he/she can make use of PSJ-Utility. While writing PSJ, user can take advantage of PSJ Customized Shell and Customized IDE to help debug code easier. The final code can run without a GUI, but if user wants to make it friendlier, PSJ-GUI then can be implemented. Macro PSJ-Command PSJ-Utility PSJ-GUI Customized shell Customized IDE Macro is equivalent to Jupiter built-in dialog function, but without GUI. For example: CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) : Make a cube with default input values ImprintLineS([[7.8, 0, 10], [2.2, 10, 10]], [6:26], 1) : Imprint a line on a face between 2 points It is generated right after a dialog function successfully runs. Macro can be recorded, run, save and reload using the Macro window. 🡆 Read more about Macro Equivalent to Macro, but PSJ-Command is polished to be compact, easy to write and fully Python compatible. This new PSJ feature is introduced from Jupiter version 5. For example: Macro PSJ-Command CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) Geometry.Part.Cube() ImprintLineS([[7.8, 0, 10], [2.2, 10, 10]], [6:26], 1) Geometry.Edge.Line(dllPoints=[[0.0078, 0, 0.01], [0.0023, 0.01, 0.01]], crlFaces=[Face(26)]) In detail, PSJ-Command has special features: Functions are named after Class-based format and Jupiter’s ribbon. Parameters are neglected if the default values are taken. Easier to read thanks to its explicit definitions. Has return value which can make the code looks more Pythonic. Has error handling built-in which can help developer found the bug faster and easier. Fully supported by our customized IDE or VSCode extensions. 🡆 Read more about PSJ-Command PSJ-Utility is used for querying model’s information. It is used to complement what is missing from the Macro or PSJ-Command. For example: JPT.Debugger(): Console debugger for PSJ. This utility will show all the related information of the inputted value to the Python API window. JPT.Exec(): Run Jupiter macro JPT.GetAllParts(): Get information of all parts PSJ-Utility is written in the form of: JPT.Function_Name(parameters) 🡆 Read more about PSJ-Utility PSJ-GUI is an UI library supporting user making dialog fast and easily. For example: dlg.add_label(name="Label30",text="Average Size",width=100,text_halign="left",text_valign="top",layout="Layout29") : Add a text label dlg.add_textbox(name="Aver_size",layout="Layout29") : Add a text edit box Different from other Python UI packages (e.g. PyQT, Tkinter, PySide, etc.), PSJ-GUI is fully integrating into Jupiter’s UI framework, help making user’s function same look & feel as Jupiter’s built-in dialog function. PSJ-GUI also supports 2-ways connection, e.g. picking, table, tab/wizard, etc. GUI Command Builder is an interactive builder of PSJ-GUI, help making Jupiter dialog or wizard by Drag & Drop operations. User hence does not need to know Python programming language to make UI components in Jupiter. 🡆 Read more about PSJ-GUI Customized shell is a Jupiter window displays PSJ output and information, with: Python API Window: Python commands and execution results are displayed. Command Line Interface (CLI): user can run Python scripts directly here. Command input is possible by Copy & Paste. 🡆 Read more about Customized Shell To write PSJ easier, we developed a Customized IDE with: Code highlighter Auto completion Tooltip for built in function or user-defined function Group block of script (Collapse/Expand) 🡆 Read more about Customized IDE Built in Python (version 3) compiler PSJ also including useful Python libraries from Python, e.g. pandas, numpy, matplotlib, pptx, scikit-learn, numba, etc. And ability to be integrated to Visual Studio Code using our customized extension.

This tutorial demonstrates how to make a custom bolt by using a pre-defined template of PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. It will also integrate the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a customized UI dialog by using GUI Command Builder. In this tutorial, you’ll learn How to get and make use of the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. Implement the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a general Python script for the automation process. Creat a dialog by using GUI Command Builder. Integrate the user script in (2.) to the created dialog in (3.) to make a custom UI function. Add the created custom UI function in (4.) to Jupiter's ribbon and use it.

About this dialog: you will make an UI dialog to integrate the customized PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro for the automation process. After selecting the bolt's size and pressing Apply or OK button (left picture), a user-standard bolt will be created and shown in Jupiter's screen (right picture). In general, below are the steps that you will follow: Get PSJ-Command or Macro: Execute the available functions in Jupiter to get the respective PSJ-Command or Macro. Create DEF function in Python: Combine PSJ-Command or Macro with Python based script in order to create an user-defined function fully. Create User Interface (UI): Use GUI Command Builder to make an UI dialog connecting to the user-defined function in (2.). Implement: Register the created UI dialog in (3.) to Jupiter.

In this section, you can learn how to get the PSJ-Command/Macro from the executed function. Within this example, you also can know how to implement the PSJ-Command/Macro of the following functions: Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function. Assemble » Assemble » Assemble Faces function. Geometry » Edit Entity » Merge Entities » Parts function. Rename the part on the Assembly window.

Use Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function to make 2 cylinders in sequence: one for bolt head, the other for bolt body. ※1. The number of the edge of the bolt head. In this case, we inputted 6 for 6 edges of the bolt head. You can change it by your own. ※2. Value of L parameter will be equal to (Height - Origin-Y), and Origin-Y will be equal to the height of bolt head - 0.005. The reason is to prevent zero-touch case. Then, you can see the created bolt on the Jupiter's display window: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Head", dTopOuterRadius=0.003005, dBottomOuterRadius=0.003005, dHeight=0.002, iCircularNodes=6) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Body", dlOrigin=[0.0, 0.001995, 0.0], dTopOuterRadius=0.0015, dBottomOuterRadius=0.0015, dHeight=0.010005, iPartColor=6409934) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Head", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0, 0], 0.001, 0.003005, 0.001, 0.003005, 0.002, 6, 10, 7105764) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Body", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0.001995, 0], 0.001, 0.0015, 0.001, 0.0015, 0.010005, 36, 10, 6409934)

Then, use Assemble » Assemble » Assemble Faces function to generate share faces between the created 2 cylinders: Input tolerance = 0.01 to the Tolerance textbox. Click on the Find button to find all the faces between the created 2 cylinders. Click on the Apply or OK button to generate share faces finding from (2.). A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assemble.FindMatingFaceEx(crlTaBodies=[Part(1, 2)], dMatingTol=1e-05) Assemble.AssembleFaceEx(ilPairFaceToMakeShareFace=[9, 3], dTolerance=1e-05, iTypeConnectPos=0) AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:1, 3:2], 1e-05) AssembleFaceEx([9, 3], 1e-05, 0, 0)

Next, use Geometry » Edit Entity » Merge Entities » Parts function to merge 2 cylinders into 1 part. This part will be considered as a simple bolt geometry using in this tutorial: Select 2 created cylinders with their shared faces. Click on the Apply or OK button to merge them into 1 part. A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.MergeEntities.Parts(crlParts=[Part(1, 2)], dMergeTolerance=1e-05) MergePart(1e-08, 1, [3:1, 3:2])

Finally, right-click on the merged part in the Assembly window to rename this part to BOLT. A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assembly.RightClick.Rename(strNewName="BOLT", crItem=Part(1)) RenameItem("BOLT", 3:1)

To recap, below is the total PSJ-Command and Macro collected in the above steps: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Head", dTopOuterRadius=0.003005, dBottomOuterRadius=0.003005, dHeight=0.002, iCircularNodes=6) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Body", dlOrigin=[0.0, 0.001995, 0.0], dTopOuterRadius=0.0015, dBottomOuterRadius=0.0015, dHeight=0.010005, iPartColor=6409934) Assemble.FindMatingFaceEx(crlTaBodies=[Part(1, 2)], dMatingTol=1e-05) Assemble.AssembleFaceEx(ilPairFaceToMakeShareFace=[9, 3], dTolerance=1e-05, iTypeConnectPos=0) Geometry.MergeEntities.Parts(crlParts=[Part(1, 2)], dMergeTolerance=1e-05) Assembly.RightClick.Rename(strNewName="BOLT", crItem=Part(1)) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Head", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0, 0], 0.001, 0.003005, 0.001, 0.003005, 0.002, 6, 10, 7105764) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Body", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0.001995, 0], 0.001, 0.0015, 0.001, 0.0015, 0.010005, 36, 10, 6409934) AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:1, 3:2], 1e-05) AssembleFaceEx([9, 3], 1e-05, 0, 0) MergePart(1e-08, 1, [3:1, 3:2]) RenameItem("BOLT", 3:1) Use the above scripts, now parameterize the numbers and add some built-in Python functions (if…else, for, while, etc.) to make the script adapt to different input parameters. To execute the code in Python, use 2 ways as below: PSJ-Command: Copy and paste directly to the creating Python code. Macro: use the following structure to execute the code in pythonJPT.Exec(“Macro”). info The PSJ-Command and/or Macro is added to create the bolt according to the value generated by user. From now, user can combine the knowledge about Python language and the just generated Macro to create def function. The following process will show you the way to prepare important def of this example:

import re from os import listdir from os.path import isfile, join from pyjdg import * import random In which: re is a library helping you to modify string. listdir, isfile, join are the libraries helping you to get all files inside a specific folder. pyjdg is a library to enable GUI Command Builder. random is a library to get a random number (for setting part's color).

documents.t: With the current output value of the Assemble Faces function, we need to modify before using it. The current output of the finding pair faces option will have the following structure (For example): 1, ["72-47"]. Or, you can understand via the following structure: 1, ["face1-face2","face3-face4","face5-face6",...] So, to make it can be used, you can use the following def function (or you can create your own function). tip Whenever start using a function, you should check it's output values and type. In Jupiter, we're supporting a utility called JPT.Debugger()Console debugger for PSJ. This utility will show all the related information of the inputted value to the Python API window. def replace_str(err, in_str): mod_str = in_str for i in range (len(err)): mod_str = mod_str.replace(str(err[i]), " ") mod_str = re.sub("s+", " ", mod_str).strip().split(" ") return mod_str

It will have the following structure: PSJ-Command Macro def on_execute_button_clicked(dlg): ''' Create a bolt when click on the Apply or OK button. Parameters: dlg: Call class dlg for using [dlg.] - API between the GUI Command Builder and Python. Results: A bolt is created when Apply or OK button is clicked. ''' # Preparing parameters for the creation part_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") coord_system = int(dlg.get_combobox_sel(name="coord_system")) bolt_type = int(dlg.get_combobox_sel(name="bolt_type")) [k, e, d] = get_bolt_size(bolt_type) # Get size of the creating bolt based on the selected bolt_type option nut_radius = e/2 thread_radius = d/2 cylinder_height = k cylinder_position = cylinder_height bolt_length = dlg.get_item_text(name="bolt_length") get_param_bolt_length = float(bolt_length)*0.001 color = random.randint(10000, 60000000) # Creating bolt head and bolt body Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName=part_name, dlOrigin=[0, 0, 0], dTopOuterRadius=nut_radius, dBottomOuterRadius=nut_radius, dHeight=cylinder_height, iCircularNodes=6, iPartColor=color) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName=part_name, dlOrigin=[0, cylinder_position, 0], dTopOuterRadius=thread_radius, dBottomOuterRadius=thread_radius, dHeight=get_param_bolt_length, iPartColor=color, crLocalCoordinate=Coord(coord_system)) # Making assemble faces all_part = sorted([a.id for a in JPT.GetAllParts()], reverse = False) assemble_face_func = JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:{0}, 3:{1}], 0.0003).' .format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) errstr = ", []-\"" JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceEx([{0}, {1}], 0.0003, 0, 0)' .format(replace_str(errstr, assemble_face_func)[-2], replace_str(errstr, assemble_face_func)[-1])) # Merging 2 created parts into 1 part JPT.Exec('MergePart(1e-05, 1, [3:{0}, 3:{1}])'.format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) # Show the created part JPT.Exec('View Fit To Model()') # Change the part_name parameter (On the GUI) automatically if str(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name")).find("_") != -1: if dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name").split("_")[-1].isdigit() == True: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name")[:-(len(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") .split("_")[-1]) + 1)] + "_" + str(int(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name").split("_")[-1]) + 1) else: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") + "_" + str(len([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]) + 1) else: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") + "_" + str(len([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]) + 1) dlg.set_item_text(name="part_name", text=new_name) def on_execute_button_clicked(dlg): ''' Creating a bolt when click on the Apply or OK button Parameters: dlg: Call class dlg for using [dlg.] - API between the GUI Command Builder and Python. Get size of the creating bolt based on the selected bolt_type option nut_radius = e/2 thread_radius = d/2 cylinder_height = k cylinder_position = cylinder_height bolt_length = dlg.get_item_text(name="bolt_length") get_param_bolt_length = float(bolt_length)*0.001 color = random.randint(10000, 60000000) # Creating bolt head and bolt body JPT.Exec('CreateCylinderPart("{0}", 27:{1}, 0, 0, [0, 0, 0], 0.001, {2}, 0.001, {2}, {3}, 6, 10, {4})' .format(part_name, coord_system, nut_radius, cylinder_height, color)) JPT.Exec('CreateCylinderPart("{0}", 27:{1}, 0, 0, [0, {2}, 0], 0.001, {3}, 0.001, {3}, {4}, 36, 10, {5})' .format(part_name, coord_system, cylinder_position, thread_radius, get_param_bolt_length, color)) # Making assemble faces errstr = ", []-\"" all_part = sorted([a.id for a in JPT.GetAllParts()], reverse = False) assemble_faces = JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:{0}, 3:{1}], 0.0003).' .format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceEx([{0}, {1}], 0.0003, 0, 0)' .format(replace_str(errstr, assemble_faces)[-2], replace_str(errstr, assemble_faces)[-1])) # Merging 2 created parts into 1 part JPT.Exec('MergePart(1e-08, 1, [3:{0}, 3:{1}])'.format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) # Show the created part only JPT.InverseHideBodies(all_part[-2]) JPT.ViewFitToModel() # To create a dialog with title and execution buttons, please do the following steps: In the opened dialog, click on the Dialog component inside the Hierarchy window. After clicking on the Dialog component (1.), change its properties as the below suggestions: 2.1. Title: Bolt Creation. 2.2. Validation: Checked on (Enable this option). 2.3. Apply Button: Checked on (Enable this option). 2.4. Ok Button: Checked on (Enable this option). 2.5. Cancel Button: Checked on (Enable this option).
documents.s: 3.2. Create a dialog with title and execution buttons

documents.t: To add the required components to the creating dialog, please follow the following steps: Add Unit System: mm by using Label component. Add an image as a preview picture into the creating dialog by using ImageCtrl component. Add Part Name textbox to input the name of the creating bolt by using Layout, Label and TextBox components. Add Coordinate System selection to select the reference coordinate system for creating bolt by using Layout, Label and ComboBox components. Add Bolt Type selection to select the reference coordinate system for creating bolt by using Layout, Label and ComboBox components. Add Update preview bolt size button to update the preview bolt picture on the GUI based on the selected bolt type by using Layout and Button components. Add Bolt Length textbox to input the length of the creating bolt by using Layout, Label and TextBox components.

After creating your own UI, you need to export it to Python file (*.py): Click on the Show or hide code window(F1) button to show/hide the UI code (Python format). Click on the Export PSJ button to export the created UI to Python file (*.py).
documents.s: 3.4. Export the created UI to python file

documents.t: After exporting the created UI to Python file (*.py), you need to bind the created def functions to the created UI. The created def functions in 2. and their corresponding are shown as below: Created def function Corresponding UI component Created component name API for binding change_bolt_pic bolt_type dlg.on_button_clicked(name="update_picture", callfunc=change_bolt_pic) on_execute_button_clicked ButtonApply dlg.on_button_clicked(name="ButtonApply", callfunc=on_execute_button_clicked) ButtonOk dlg.on_button_clicked(name="ButtonOk", callfunc=on_execute_button_clicked)

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to capture model image without screen effect: Take a screenshot of the current viewed model and output to a *.jpg file. Disable screen update, screen animation and message output to Macro/Python API window to improve PSJ performance. Notice Avoid using JPT.Disable... functions in a loop. Once disabled, it will affect until it is enabled again.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() import time import os start = time.time() # Turn off output message to Macro and Python API windows # It will be automatically enabled again after PSJ finishes running JPT.DisableOutputMessage() # Disable screen animation (It is necessary when you capture model on the Visualization window) # It will be automatically enabled again after PSJ finishes running JPT.DisableScreenAnimation() # Prepare a cube Geometry.Part.Cube() # Capture model image and output it to your local folder JPT.ViewFitToModel() strDesktopPath = os.path.join(os.path.join(os.environ['USERPROFILE']), 'Desktop') strImagePath = strDesktopPath + "/cube_image.jpg" Home.ToImage(strImgPath=strImagePath) # Collapse assembly tree window to avoid GUI update JPT.CollapseAssemblyTree() # Start transaction point JPT.BeginDatabaseTransaction("Change element color operation") # Change color of all elements for elem in JPT.GetAllElems(): elem.color = JPT.GetRandomJPTColor() # End transaction point JPT.EndDatabaseTransaction() # Capture the current model image and output it to your local folder strNewImagePath = strDesktopPath + "/cube_new_image.jpg" Home.ToImage(strImgPath=strNewImagePath) # Enable screen animation JPT.EnableScreenAnimation() # Turn on output message to Macro and Python API windows JPT.EnableOutputMessage() # Get the execution time elapsed_time = time.time() - start print('Time Total: ' + str(elapsed_time) +'s')

This tutorial demonstrates how to create a model and setting boundary conditions for plan stress problem by using a pre-defined template of PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. After that, using TS-SunShine to solve the plane stress problem exporting from Jupiter. It will also integrates the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a customized UI dialog by using GUI Command Builder. In this tutorial, you’ll learn How to get and make use of the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. Implement the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a general Python script for the automation process. Call TS-SunShine to solve the exported file from Jupiter. Open powerpoint and put the outputted values to powerpoint to create a report. Creat a dialog by using GUI Command Builder. Integrate the user script in (2.) to the created dialog in (3.) to make a custom UI function. Add the created custom UI function in (4.) to Jupiter's ribbon and use it.

About this dialog: you will make an UI dialog to integrate the customized PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro for the automation process. After inputting values and clicking on the Apply/OK button, user can get the report containing the result of the created model. In general, below are the steps that you will follow: Get PSJ-Command or Macro: Executing available functions in Jupiter to get the respective PSJ-Command or Macro. Create DEF function in Python: Combining PSJ-Command or Macro with Python based script in order to create a full user function. Create User Interface (UI): Using GUI Command Builder to make an UI dialog connecting to the user function in (2.). Implement: Registering the created UI dialog in (3.) to Jupiter.

In this section, you can learn how to get the PSJ-Command/Macro from the executed function. Within this example, you also can know how to implement the PSJ-Command/Macro of the following functions: Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cube function. Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function. Assemble » Combination » Boolean function. Geometry » Delete Entity » Face function. Meshing » Surface Meshing function. Properties » Material function. Properties » Shell function. Boundary Conditions » Constraints » Fixed Constraints function. Boundary Conditions » Force » General function. Analysis » TSSS function. Undo command by using Ctrl + Z Renaming part on the Assembly window.

Using Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cube function to make a cube using as the base model of the plane stress model. Then, you can see the created cube on the Jupiter's display window: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cube(dlLength=[0.02, 0.001, 0.015], strName="planestress_model1", iPartColor=7531634) CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [0.02, 0.001, 0.015], [10, 10, 10], "planestress_model1", 7531634, 0:0)

Using Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function to make a cylinder for making a hole in the center of the plan stress model. Then, you can see the created cylinder and the created cube on 1.1. on the Jupiter's display window: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cylinder(dlOrigin=[0.01, -0.001, 0.0075], dTopRadius=0.001, dBottomRadius=0.001, dHeight=0.003, iPartColor=7697908) CreateCylinderFrustum([0.01, -0.001, 0.0075], 0.001, 0.001, 0.003, 36, 10, "Cylinder_1", 7697908, 0:0)

Using Assemble » Combination » Boolean function and select Subtract option to make a hole in the center of the plane stress model. This function will use the created cylinder (Step 1.1.) and the created cube (Step 1.2.). After using this function, the creating model will be the same as below: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assemble.BooleanEx([Part(1, 2)], strNameSuffix="", iBooleanType=1) BooleanEx([3:1, 3:2], "", 1, 0, 0, 0)

Then, you can see the new name of the subtracted part: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assembly.RightClick.Rename(strNewName="planstress_model1", crItem=Part(1)) RenameItem("planstress_model1", 3:1)

Using Geometry » Delete Entity » Delete Entity » Face function to create plane stress model by deleting all the unnecessary faces. Then, you can see the model after deleling faces: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.DeleteEntity.Face([Face(31, 22, 25, 23, 26, 24)]) DeleteFaceCr([6:31, 6:22, 6:25, 6:23, 6:26, 6:24], 1)

tip Before executing Surface Meshing function, you should enable Show mesh line option. This operation will let you see the mesh line. Using Meshing » Meshing » Surface Meshing function and select Tri3 option to create plane stress model by deleting all the unnecessary faces. Then, you can see the model after meshing: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Meshing.SetMeshAttribute(crlPart=[Part(1)], surfaceMesh=SURFACE_MESH(dAvgElemSize=0.002, dMaxElemSize=0.003, dMinElemSize=0.0001, dGeomAngle=0.7853981634, dGeomMinSize=0.0001, iPerformanceMode=1, dAutoMergeTinyFacesAngle=0.5235987756, bGeomApprox=True, iNextEntityOffsetId=0)) Meshing.SurfaceMeshing(crlPart=[Part(1)], surfaceMesh=SURFACE_MESH(dAvgElemSize=0.002, dMaxElemSize=0.003, dMinElemSize=0.0001, dGeomAngle=0.7853981634, dGeomMinSize=0.0001, iPerformanceMode=1, dAutoMergeTinyFacesAngle=0.5235987756, bGeomApprox=True, iNextEntityOffsetId=0), iThreadNum=4) MeshEditAdjustVertex([3:1]) SetMeshAttrib([3:1], {0.002, 0.003, 0.0001, 1, 0.7853981634, 0.0001, 1.25, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.5, 1, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0.5235987756, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 10000000, 0, 0}) SurfaceMeshing2D([3:1], {0.002, 0.003, 0.0001, 1, 0.7853981634, 0.0001, 1.25, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.5, 1, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0.5235987756, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 10000000, 0, 0}, 1, 0, 4, 1, 0, 65280) note After executing Surface Meshing function, you need to convert the meshed model to first/second order. First order A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro ElementConv_Surface([3:1], 0) MeshEdit.SurfaceMesh(crlPart=[Part(1)], iType=0) Second order A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro ElementConv_Surface([3:1], 1) MeshEdit.SurfaceMesh(crlPart=[Part(1)])

PSJ GUI EXAMPLES # --------------------- # This example demonstrades how to apply PSJ on a simple problem # such as plane stress problem # Required: Sunshine license #******************************************************************************* import JPT import re import os from pyjdg import * import random import ctypes import subprocess def cnvt_str_to_list(in_str: str) -> list: err_chars = r"/¥|^[]()" split_char = "," in_str = in_str.strip(err_chars) in_str = in_str.split(split_char) return in_str def convert_to_dbody(macro_tcursor: str): return JPT.CastDItemToDBody(JPT.MacroTCursorToDItem(str(macro_tcursor))) def create_geometry(part_name, get_width, get_height, get_radius): JPT.ClearLog() try: type_tobe_deleted = [3, 22] for type_id in type_tobe_deleted: for item in JPT.GetAllByTypeID(type_id): JPT.Exec('DeleteItem(0, [{0}:{1}], [], [], 1)'.format(type_id, item.id)) if part_name == "": part_name = "Plane_Stress_1" cube_size_x = float(get_width) * 0.001 cube_size_z = float(get_height) * 0.001 cube_size_h = 1e-3 hole_rad = float(get_radius) * 0.001 if cube_size_x > 0 and cube_size_z > 0 and hole_rad > 0: color = random.randint(10000, 60000000) create_cube = convert_to_dbody(Geometry.Part.Cube(dlLength=[cube_size_x, cube_size_h, cube_size_z], strName=part_name, iPartColor=color)) part_pos_x = 0 + cube_size_x / 2 part_pos_z = 0 + cube_size_z / 2 cylinder_height = cube_size_h + 2e-3 create_cylinder = Geometry.Part.Cylinder(dlOrigin=[part_pos_x, -0.001, part_pos_z], dTopRadius=hole_rad, dBottomRadius=hole_rad, dHeight=cylinder_height, iPartColor=color) # Get part ID Assemble.BooleanEx([Part(create_cube.id, max([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]))], strNameSuffix="", iBooleanType=1) create_cube.name = part_name # Get ID of face all_face_id = [(str(_.typeID)) + ":" + (str(_.id)) for _ in JPT.GetAllFaces()] target_face = [] for cursor in all_face_id: str_command = 'EntityInfo({0},"CENTER")'.format(cursor) coordinate = cnvt_str_to_list(JPT.Exec(str_command))[1] # Select the coordinate value according to Y direction if float(coordinate) > 0: target_face.append(cursor) # Delete the unnecessary face res = [int(_.split(":")[-1]) for _ in target_face] # Change from list [6:1, 6:2, ...] --> list [1, 2] JPT.Exec('DeleteFace({}, 1)'.format(res)) JPT.ViewFitToModel() JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Created model information: ") print("--- Part name: %s" %str(part_name)) print("--- Width: %s mm" %str(get_width)) print("--- Height: %s mm" %str(get_height)) print("--- Hole radius: %s mm" %str(get_radius)) print("==================================================================") else: print("==================================================================") print("** [ERROR OCCURED] **") print("Inputted values are wrong, please check again!") print("The inputted values should follow the following rules:!") print("--- First: Model size should not be blanked. Its means you need to input float numbers") print("--- Second: The inputted values must be bigger than 0") print("==================================================================") except ValueError: print("==================================================================") print("** [ERROR OCCURED] **") print("Inputted values are wrong, please check again!") print("The inputted values should follow the following rules:!") print("--- First: Model size should not be blanked. Its means you need to input float numbers") print("--- Second: The inputted values must be bigger than 0") print("==================================================================") def clear_geometry(): JPT.ClearLog() for part in JPT.GetAllByTypeID(3): JPT.Exec('DeleteItem(0, [3:{}], [], [], 1)'.format(part.id)) JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Deleted all the created parts!") print("==================================================================") def generate_meshing(avg_size, min_size, max_size, second_element): try: JPT.ClearLog() JPT.Exec('ViewShowMesh(1)') avg_size_mm = float(avg_size) * 0.001 min_size_mm = float(min_size) * 0.001 max_size_mm = float(max_size) * 0.001 if min_size_mm < 0.7*avg_size_mm and min_size_mm > 0 and \ max_size_mm > 1.4*avg_size_mm and max_size_mm > 0 and \ avg_size_mm > 0: for part in JPT.GetAllParts(): Meshing.SurfaceMeshing(crlPart=[Part(part.id)], surfaceMesh=SURFACE_MESH(dAvgElemSize=avg_size_mm, dMaxElemSize=max_size_mm, dMinElemSize=min_size_mm, dGeomAngle=0.7853981634, dGeomMinSize=0.0001, dMinStretchVal=0.01, iPerformanceMode=1, dAutoMergeTinyFacesAngle=0.5235987756, bGeomApprox=True, iNextEntityOffsetId=0), iThreadNum=12) if second_element == True: MeshEdit.SurfaceMesh(crlPart=[Part(part.id)]) element_type = "Tri3 (First order)" if second_element == False else "Tri6 (Second order)" JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Meshed model information: ") print("--- Average size: %s mm" %str(avg_size)) print("--- Minimum size: %s mm" %str(min_size)) print("--- Maximum size: %s mm" %str(max_size)) print("--- Element type: %s" %str(element_type)) print("==================================================================") else: print("==================================================================") print("** [ERROR OCCURED] **") print("Inputted values are wrong, please check again!") print("The inputted values should follow the following rules:!") print("--- First: All the inputted values must be bigger than 0") print("--- Second: Minimum size is less than or equal to 0.7*[Average size]") print("--- Third: Maximum size is more than or equal to 1.4*[Average size]") print("==================================================================") except ValueError: print("==================================================================") print("** [ERROR OCCURED] **") print("Inputted values are wrong, please check again!") print("The inputted values should follow the following rules:!") print("--- First: All the inputted values must be bigger than 0") print("--- Second: Minimum size is less than or equal to 0.7*[Average size]") print("--- Third: Maximum size is more than or equal to 1.4*[Average size]") print("==================================================================") def undo_meshing(): JPT.ClearLog() Toolbar.Undo(iCntUndo=3) JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Removed surface meshing successfully!") print("==================================================================") def apply_property(dlg): JPT.ClearLog() check = False for prop in JPT.GetAllByTypeID(87): for entities in prop.targets: if entities.typeID == 3: check = True print("The current plane stress model is having material property") print("Please click Clear button before applying the new one") break if check == True: break if check == False: sel_mat = dlg.get_combobox_sel('list_material') thickness = 1e-6 part_id = [_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()][0] mat_name = "" if sel_mat == 0: # Copper Alloy mat_name = "Copper Alloy" Properties.Material.Add("Copper_Alloy", [Density([(DENSITY, 8.3e-09)]), Elastic([(YOUNGS_MODULUS, 110000.0), (POISSONS_RATIO, 0.34)])]) if sel_mat == 1: # Manesium Alloy mat_name = "Manesium Alloy" Properties.Material.Add("Magnesium_Alloy", [Density([(DENSITY, 1.8e-09)]), Elastic([(YOUNGS_MODULUS, 45000.0), (POISSONS_RATIO, 0.35)])]) if sel_mat == 2: # Concrete mat_name = "Concrete" Properties.Material.Add("Concrete", [Density([(DENSITY, 2.3e-09)]), Elastic([(YOUNGS_MODULUS, 30000.0), (POISSONS_RATIO, 0.18)])]) if sel_mat == 3: # Structure Steel mat_name = "Structure Steel" Steel" Properties.Material.Add("Stainless_Steel", [Density([(DENSITY, 7.75e-09)]), Elastic([(YOUNGS_MODULUS, 193000.0), (POISSONS_RATIO, 0.31)])]) command2='Property2DShell("Plane_Stress_Example", 1, 22:{0}, 22:{0}, 22:{0}, 0:0, \ 1.79769e+308, 1.79769e+308, 1.79769e+308, {1}, 1.79769e+308, \ 1.79769e+308, 1.79769e+308, 1.79769e+308, 1.79769e+308, 1.79769e+308, 2147483647, 0, 0:0, [3:{2}], 0:0, 0)'.\ format((sel_mat + 1), thickness, part_id) JPT.Exec(command2) JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Applied material: %s" %str(mat_name)) print("==================================================================") def clear_property(): JPT.ClearLog() for prop in JPT.GetAllByTypeID(87): JPT.Exec('DeleteItem(0, [87:{}], [], [], 1)'.format(prop.id)) JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Deleted all the applied material properties!") print("==================================================================") def apply_fixed_constraint(constraint_name, x_direction, z_direction): JPT.ClearLog() constraint_dir = "" selected_edges = "" for edge in JPT.GetSelectedEdges(): if x_direction == True: constraint_dir = "X" contraint_type = 59 if z_direction == True: constraint_dir = "Z" contraint_type = 62 if x_direction == True and z_direction == True: constraint_dir = "X and Z" contraint_type = 63 BoundaryConditions.FixedConstraint(strName=constraint_name, iDwDof=contraint_type, crlTargets=[Edge(edge.id)]) selected_edges += 1)'.format(force.id)) JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Deleted all the applied forces!") In this tutorial, you'll learn how to export a simple report (pptx - Powerpoint format) by using python-pptx library with PSJ: Read the model information (part ID, part name, number of nodes, elements, faces, edges, etc.). Make a table comparing the above information. Append the content to a PowerPoint file with pre-defined template: First slide: title with created date. Second slide: model information table.

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 import JPT from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN from os.path import isfile, isdir from pptx import Presentation from pptx.util import Inches from pptx.util import Pt from pptx.enum.text import MSO_ANCHOR from datetime import datetime import re # Change your template and output folder here template_file = r"C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\template\template_report.pptx" output_folder = r"C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\template" def export_report(template_file = "", output_folder = "", num_of_cols = 8): if isfile(template_file) and isdir(output_folder): # Output report file template_file = re.sub(re.escape("\\"), "/", template_file) output_pptx_file = re.sub(re.escape("\\"), "/", output_folder + "/" + "modal_infor_report.pptx") # Open template report and store it to a parameter ppt_report = Presentation(template_file) # Create the first slide (Title slide) title_slide = ppt_report.slides.add_slide(ppt_report.slide_layouts[0]) title_slide.shapes.title.text = "EXAMPLE FOR EXPORTING MODAL INFORMATION" title_slide.placeholders[1].text = "Created: " + \ str(datetime.now().year) + \ "." + \ str(datetime.now().month) + \ "." + \ str(datetime.now().day) # Create the 2nd slide (Modal info slide) slide = ppt_report.slides.add_slide(ppt_report.slide_layouts[4]) slide.shapes.title.text = "MODAL INFORMATION" x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(10), Inches(2) table = slide.shapes.add_table(len(JPT.GetAllParts()) + 2, num_of_cols, x, y, cx, cy).table table.cell(0, 0).merge(table.cell(0, num_of_cols - 1)) table.cell(0, 0).text = "Modal information" table.cell(1, 0).text = "Part ID" table.cell(1, 1).text = "Part Name" table.cell(1, 2).text = "No. of Faces" table.cell(1, 3).text = "No. of Edges" table.cell(1, 4).text = "No. of Elements" table.cell(1, 5).text = "No. of Nodes" table.cell(1, 6).text = "Range of Node ID" table.cell(1, 7).text = "Range of Element ID" table.columns[0].width = Inches(1.2) table.columns[1].width = Inches(1.9) table.columns[2].width = Inches(1.2) table.columns[3].width = Inches(1.2) table.columns[4].width = Inches(1.5) table.columns[5].width = Inches(1.5) table.columns[6].width = Inches(1.9) table.columns[7].width = Inches(1.9) if len(JPT.GetAllParts()): for row, part in enumerate(JPT.GetAllParts()): table.cell(row + 2, 0).text = str(part.id) table.cell(row + 2, 1).text = part.name table.cell(row + 2, 2).text = str(len(part.faces)) table.cell(row + 2, 3).text = str(len(part.edges)) table.cell(row + 2, 4).text = str(len(part.elems)) table.cell(row + 2, 5).text = str(len(part.nodes)) table.cell(row + 2, 6).text = "Max: " + \ str(max([_.id for _ in part.nodes])) + \ "\n" + \ "Min: " + \ str(min([_.id for _ in part.nodes])) table.cell(row + 2, 7).text = "Max: " + \ str(max([_.id for _ in part.elems])) + \ "\n" + \ "Min: " + \ str(min([_.id for _ in part.elems])) table.rows[row].height = Inches(0.53) for row in table.rows: for cell in row.cells: cell.vertical_anchor = MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs: paragraph.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER for run in paragraph.runs: run.font.size = Pt(13) run.font.name = "MS UI Gothic" ppt_report.save(output_pptx_file) print(" FINISHED ".center(100, "*")) else: print("Error: template file and/or output folder does not exist!")
